summary.title: How HashiCorp Works
summary.one_liner: A collection of HashiCorp's documented individual, manager/team, and company practices, including remote work, decision-making through writing, meetings, feedback, hiring, and goal-setting templates.
takeaways: HashiCorp documents its implicit cultural norms and working practices as explicit, open-source guides.
Individual practices cover writing-based decision making, employee relationships, remote-first work habits, and data-driven success expectations.
Manager and team guidance includes a standardized manager development program and best practices for different meeting types.
Templates are provided for Scorecards (annual goals with quarterly reviews), RFCs (proposing solutions and gathering feedback), and PRDs (defining problems and requirements).
summary.summary: The site is HashiCorp's open-sourced handbook, started as an internal resource for new employees to make unwritten practices explicit. It is organized into three sections: individual practices (writing, remote work, data-driven expectations), manager and team practices (manager development, meetings, feedback), and company practices (hiring, operating cadence, culture), plus a resources section with Scorecard, RFC, and PRD templates. Per the About section, the guides are updated yearly and some reference internal documents that were kept for consistency. The page itself is an index of guides, so the details live in each linked article.
